title: Route latency quantile slices and approximate join fabric
creator: Marco Li
description: Produce a compact, query-friendly representation of latency distributions per tenant+route that supports fast percentile queries for dashboards and SLO evaluation. The goal is to avoid full raw-event scans for 95/99/99.9p while preserving actionable accuracy for alerts and heatmaps. Deliverables: (1) hourly materialized quantile slices (compact sketch blobs), (2) an approximate-join fabric that can stitch sketches to route/tenant metadata and cost facts, (3) SQL UDFs for approximate percentile and differential comparisons used by Console and downstream alerts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Queries for p50/p95/p99 on daily and weekly windows complete under 2s for interactive panels using the quantile slices. 2) Storage cost for the quantile layer within 10% of initial projection (benchmark below). 3) Integration tests demonstrate <1% error vs raw-rollup baselines on synthetic workloads for p95 and p99 across the 10k tenant sample. 4) Rollout gating: feature flag enabled for 10% of tenants and A/B comparison shows parity for SLO trigger rates.
implementation_notes: We evaluated t-digest, KLL, and histogram sketches during the spike. KLL sketches give better tail stability at small sketch sizes; we will standardize on KLL with 256 or 512 items depending on route traffic. Store sketches as base64-encoded protobuf blobs in a compact materialized table partitioned by hour and tenant_id. Use Spark / SparkSQL for nightly incremental compaction and BigQuery or Redshift (depending on cluster) for serving materialized views via external tables. Provide SQL UDF wrapper for percent_rank(sketch, q) and sketch_merge(sketches[]). Use winsorization at 99.99p on raw per-invocation latency to guard against measurement anomalies. To enable approximate joins, create a join fabric table that maps route_id -> latest_model_version and route_labels; lookups will be broadcasted to the aggregation job to tag sketches with route metadata.
data_model: quantile_slices(hour TIMESTAMP, tenant_id STRING, route_id STRING, sketch_proto STRING, count BIGINT, sample_count BIGINT)
retention_and_cost: Keep hourly slices for 90 days, roll hourly->daily compacted sketches for 2 years, then drop to aggregated monthly sketches for 5 years. Initial storage estimate: 180k routes * 24 hours * 90 days * 1kB per sketch ~ ~3.9 GB (post-compression). Compaction job reduces serving table size by ~4x for daily artifacts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): build tables and UDFs, enable for internal tenants and CI; Phase 2 (10% customers): enable feature flag, run parallel comparisons against raw-rollups; Phase 3 (full): switch dashboards to use approximate endpoints and remove heavy raw scans. Provide automatic fallback to raw-rollups for tenants with insufficient sketch density.
testing_plan: Unit tests for KLL serialization/deserialization and merge semantics. Nightly synthetic replay test that injects known distributions and asserts quantile error tolerances. Performance test to validate query latency SLAs using a cached materialized endpoint. E2E QA to validate alerting parity on staging with mirrored traffic.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: Add new quantile_slices table without modifying existing schemas. Consumers can opt-in via feature flag. For tenants with historical raw data, run a backfill job to generate slices for the last 30 days; backfill is designed to be idempotent and chunked by tenant to avoid long-running locks.
